question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician because of increased frequency of urination. He also says that he needs to urinate 4 to 5 times nightly and has difficulty initiating a urinary stream. He has had several episodes of acute cystitis treated with ciprofloxacin during the past year. Digital rectal examination shows a firm, symmetrically enlarged, non-tender prostate. This patient is most likely to develop which of the following complications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "possible bladder outlet obstruction" -> "increased risk of urinary tract infections" -> "possible renal complications" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "increased pressure on bladder" -> "possible renal damage" -> "irreversible decrease in renal function" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "increased risk of bladder infections" -> "possible progression to pyelonephritis" -> "inflammation of renal interstitium" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "possible development of prostate abscess" -> "abscess formation in the prostate" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "possible bladder outlet obstruction" -> "increased risk of bladder dysfunction" -> "impaired intracavernosal blood flow" -> 65%

CHAIN: "Enlarged prostate" -> "increased urinary frequency" -> "difficulty initiating urinary stream" -> "risk of urinary retention" -> "possible development of prostate abscess" -> "possible systemic infection" -> "blastic bone lesions" -> "possible" -> 50%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and examination findings suggest benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) with urinary retention, which can lead to complications such as bladder outlet obstruction. This can subsequently cause renal complications due to increased pressure in the urinary tract, potentially leading to hydronephrosis and irreversible decrease in renal function. The other options are less likely given the clinical scenario.
